allies.rationale_text: Opportunity-cost sharpens comparative-advantage by showing what is lost when work stays with the wrong owner.
allies.affinity_rationale: Foundational concept — opportunity cost IS what makes comparative advantage calculable; without understanding what is lost when work stays with the wrong owner, the allocation decision has no basis.
allies.activation_condition: When task or resource allocation needs to account for what is being sacrificed elsewhere by keeping work with its current owner rather than reallocating by relative efficiency

allies.rationale_text: Specialization gives comparative-advantage the concentrated expertise that makes role reallocation worth doing.
allies.source_quote: specialization, efficiency, and leveraging unique strengths
allies.affinity_rationale: Practical output — 'specialization, efficiency, and leveraging unique strengths' — specialization is what comparative advantage produces when properly applied, but is a consequence rather than a constitutive mechanism.
allies.activation_condition: When identifying comparative advantages reveals opportunities for concentrated expertise that would make role reallocation more productive than generalist distribution

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias makes comparative-advantage defend an existing role map even after the evidence says the allocation is wrong.
antagonists.source_quote: preventing them from detecting contradictory information
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Blocks reallocation — 'preventing them from detecting contradictory information' — causes teams to defend existing role allocations even when evidence shows the current distribution is suboptimal.
antagonists.activation_condition: When evidence suggests the current task allocation is suboptimal but the team is defending the existing role map based on familiarity or politics rather than comparative efficiency

structured_tensions.tension_text: Comparative-advantage conflicts with status-quo-bias when legacy role allocation blocks higher-leverage specialization.
Comparative-advantage conflicts with commitment-bias when sunk ownership prevents reallocating tasks by marginal efficiency.
